question: Do the cars have to keep their headlights on during the day?
expected_answer: Yes. The two main headlights and the rear lights must be on permanently, by day and by night, on track and in the pit lane.

question: What language do the teams have to speak on the radio?
expected_answer: English only, unless the WEC Committee grants an exception.

question: Are cars allowed to drive backwards in the pit lane?
expected_answer: No. Using reverse gear is prohibited in the pit lane.

question: What happens if a driver collects too many penalty points?
expected_answer: Each driver has a reserve of 10 points; once it is used up, the driver is automatically suspended for the next Competition (up to 4 points can be withdrawn per Competition).

question: Can a team add fuel to a car that has stopped out on the circuit?
expected_answer: No. Any replenishment of energy or liquid on the track is prohibited; penalty: disqualification.

question: If a car breaks down on the circuit, can the team come and fix it?
expected_answer: No. Away from the garage area and the grid, repairs must be done by the driver alone with the tools and parts carried on board, and only the driver may touch a stopped car; penalty: disqualification.

question: Is a driver allowed to push his car back to the pits?
expected_answer: No, under no circumstances, not even in the pit lane; penalty: disqualification.

question: Are tyre warmers allowed?
expected_answer: No. Any thermal or heat retention device, and any attempt to change tyre temperature, is forbidden; teams may not even have such devices.

question: How many sets of tyres can a team keep inside the garage?
expected_answer: At most 3 sets per car inside the garage (front part), all visible from the pit lane; the others are stored behind the garage.

question: Do teams have to leave their garage open so people can see the car?
expected_answer: Yes. Pit curtains must stay open from 1 hour before the first session to 1 hour after the last one each day, and at least from 10:00 to 18:00, with the car visible.

question: What does the green light on a hybrid car mean?
expected_answer: The car is electrically safe. A red light or no light means the car needs immediate assistance from its team.

question: Can a team bring a spare car to a race?
expected_answer: No. Reserve cars are not admitted.

question: Do the most successful teams get handicapped?
expected_answer: A success handicap may be imposed on Hypercar and LMGT3 entries at all Competitions except the 24 Hours of Le Mans, turned into mass and/or power through the BoP.

question: How many warm-up laps are there before the race starts?
expected_answer: 2 formation laps (the Race Director may add more or decide on only one).

question: If a race is stopped and never restarted, do the teams still get points?
expected_answer: No points if the leader completed fewer than 2 green laps; half points if more than 2 laps but less than 75% of the race time; full points beyond 75%.

question: What happens if two drivers finish the season with the same number of points?
expected_answer: The one with the most wins ranks higher, then the most second places, then third places, and so on, with further tie-breakers after that.

question: Can drivers walk around the circuit before the race?
expected_answer: Only during the 'track walk' time window in the official timetable, on foot or with non-motorised transport.

question: What happens to a car that causes a red flag in qualifying?
expected_answer: All its lap times from that qualifying session are deleted (except exceptional circumstances), and it may not be allowed back into qualifying.

question: How fast can cars go when a red flag comes out in practice?
expected_answer: 80 km/h maximum, proceeding with extreme caution to the pits.

question: Can a team make a pit stop during a Full Course Yellow?
expected_answer: The pit entry closes; only an emergency stop (8 s of fuel and/or a damaged tyre) or an intervention that costs at least one lap is allowed, otherwise a 3-minute Stop & Go.

question: Can a team change which driver starts the race after qualifying?
expected_answer: Yes, if the change is notified in writing to the Stewards at the latest 30 minutes after the end of Hyperpole.

question: How is a driver's time behind the wheel counted?
expected_answer: As the sum of the driver's stints, measured between timing loops; pit stops and red-flag suspensions are excluded.

question: What happens if one of the drivers in a crew never drives during the race?
expected_answer: The car is disqualified, except in a case of force majeure recognised by the Stewards.

question: What if the chequered flag is shown too early by mistake?
expected_answer: The race is deemed to have finished when the leader last crossed the line before the flag; if it is shown late, the race ends at the scheduled time.

question: Can a car carry on driving round after it has seen the chequered flag?
expected_answer: No. It cannot cross the finish line again unless the Race Director instructs otherwise.

question: What does a drive-through penalty mean?
expected_answer: The driver must drive through the pit lane without stopping, within four crossings of the Line after notification; it cannot be appealed.

question: Can a team sell its entry to another team?
expected_answer: No. Transferring an entry is prohibited.

question: If a car isn't selected for the championship, does the team get its entry fee back?
expected_answer: Yes, the entry fee is reimbursed except €1,000 kept as handling costs.

question: How many team members can stand on the pit wall?
expected_answer: At most 3 people per car in the signalling area.

question: Can the driver stay in the car while it is being refuelled?
expected_answer: Yes, the driver may remain on board during refuelling.

question: And for LMGT3?

history.content: How many dry-weather tyres can a Hypercar use for qualifying and the race at a 6-hour race?
18 dry-weather tyres (Article 6.5.4).

expected_standalone: How many dry-weather tyres can an LMGT3 car use for qualifying and the race at a 6-hour race?
expected_answer: 24 dry-weather tyres.

question: What about at Le Mans?

history.content: How many points does the winner of a 6-hour race score?
25 points (Article 15.3.1).

expected_standalone: How many points does the winner of the 24 Hours of Le Mans score?
expected_answer: 50 points (Le Mans is also governed by its own Supplementary Regulations, Article 1.2.4).

question: Can I still go into the pits?

history.content: What is the speed limit under a Full Course Yellow?
80 km/h (Article 14.5.1).

expected_standalone: Can a car enter the pits during a Full Course Yellow?
expected_answer: The pit entry is closed; only an emergency stop or an intervention costing at least one lap is allowed.

question: And what's the penalty if I go over it in the race?

history.content: What is the speed limit in the pit lane?
60 km/h (Article 12.1.4).

expected_standalone: What is the penalty for speeding in the pit lane during the race?
expected_answer: Drive-through for the 1st and 2nd infringement below 70 km/h; Stop & Go of 5 s per km/h above 70 km/h; from the 3rd, at the Stewards' discretion.

question: And can a Bronze driver be in the crew?

history.content: What driver licence do you need to race in Hypercar?
FIA Grade A (Article 3.1.6).

expected_standalone: Can a Bronze driver be part of a Hypercar crew?
expected_answer: No. Hypercar crews must not include a Bronze driver.

question: When and where is it this year?

history.content: Is the Prologue test mandatory?
Yes, for all cars entered for the full season (Article 8.1.2).

expected_standalone: When and where is the 2026 Prologue test?
expected_answer: 22 or 23 March 2026, in Qatar.

question: Can a team appeal it?

history.content: What is a Stop & Go penalty?
The car stops in its working area, waits if a time is set, and leaves; the driver stays on board (Article 7.4.3).

expected_standalone: Can a Stop & Go penalty be appealed?
expected_answer: No. Stop & Go penalties are not subject to appeal.

question: And to appeal?

history.content: How much does it cost to lodge a protest?
A €1,000 deposit (Article 7.2.6).

expected_standalone: How much is the appeal deposit?
expected_answer: €6,000 for the International Court of Appeal.

question: Are they allowed to use tools while refuelling?

history.content: How many people can work on the car during a pit stop?
Up to four people wearing the right armband (Article 12.2.2).

expected_standalone: Can mechanics use tools while the car is being refuelled during a pit stop?
expected_answer: No. Tools are not allowed during the refuelling phase.

question: And in a 10-hour race?
